Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput Order On Board 12/10/2023

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 (for short "the Act of 1988") has been filed by the Insurance Company, being aggrieved by the award dated 16.01.2017 passed in Motor Accident Claims Case No.185/2016 by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur,
District Surguja (CG).
2.

entities.text:
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur,
District Surguja
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the claim application, the deceased namely Arvind Toppo aged about 20 years was working as helper in Laxmi Borewell Ambikapur and was earning Rs. 9,000/- per month.

On the date of accident ie. 01.07.2016 he was travelling in the offending vehicle bearing registration No.
15/AE-3090 which met with an accident and turned turtle as a result of which he died on the spot as he fall beneath the offending vehicle.
3. The claimants claimed Rs. 17,08,000/-.
Respondents /driver and owner filed its written statement barring the admitted facts, denied the averments of the claim application.

He further pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving license and the vehicle was duly insured with the Insurance Company hence, liable to pay compensation is upon it.
4. Insurance Company also filed its written statement and admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with it however denied the averments of the rest of the claim application.

It was pleaded that the deceased was not an employee of the offending vehicle rather he was an employee of the boring machine which was attached to the vehicle Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:25617 and he was travelling as a gratuitous passenger and no extra premium was paid.

The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license neither any permit fitness was available of the offending vehicle hence, there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy,
Insurance Company may be exonerated from paying the compensation.
5. Four issues were framed with regard to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle ie. violation of the insurance policy, amount of compensation and relief and cost.
Issues were decided in favour of the claimants/respondent No.1 to 3 and award of Rs. 7,79,000/- as compensation was awarded.
The finding with regard to negligence and amount of compensation has not been challenged by any of the parties
therefore attained finality.
6. The issue with regard to violation of the policy is being assailed by the Insurance Company before this Court in this appeal.

7. Shri Pankaj Agrawal and Ms. Swati Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant vehemently argued that from the evidence brought on record it is established that the deceased was not the employee of the Insured/offending vehicle rather he was employed in the boring machine which was attached to the offending vehicle therefore his risk was not covered.
They submitted that from the statement of the owner himself the above facts are clearly been established.

The deceased was traveling as a The Branch Manager, The Oriental ... vs Birbal Toppo on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153883432/

sentences.text: gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle and the risk of gratuitous passenger is not required to be covered under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, of 1988.
Therefore, the appeal may be allowed and the Insurance company may be exonerated from Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:25617 paying the compensation.

They submitted that apart from the deceased, 7-8 people were seated and therefore there was more people than the coverage in the policy were seated therefore the Insurance Company cannot be held liable.

8. Shri Sushil Dubey, learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal with regard to the violation of the Insurance Policy under Issue No.2 is fully justified.
He submits that the Insurance Company could not prove its defence by a cogent and prudent evidence and therefore no interference on this finding is required.
9. Ms.Priyanka Mehta, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.5 owner submits that the finding is absolutely justified and based upon proper appreciation of evidence.

She read over the statement of the witness of the Insurance Company, Ankit (NAW-2) to demonstrate that in his statement he has not stated anything with regard to the violation of the policy rather admitted that the premium of Rs. 150 was charged covering the risk of driver, cleaner and conductor.
She further goes on to submit that once the premium has been accepted by the Insurance company, it cannot escape its liability to pay the compensation.

She read over the statement of the owner to substantiate the fact that the vehicle attached with the boring machine was insured by the Insurance Company and the boring machine itself cannot be operated without its being installed on the offending vehicle and the offending vehicle is in a starting mode.

She further submits that the owner of the offending vehicle as well as the boring machine is the owner/respondent No.5 and no distinction can be made with Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:25617 regard to the employment either in the boring machine or in the offending vehicle.

There cannot be a separate existence of the boring machine until and unless it is attached therefore this technical plea taken by the appellant that the deceased was the employee of the boring machine cannot be accepted.

10. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the records.
11.
The core question involved in this case is whether the deceased was employee of the boring machine or offending vehicle.

12. In the claim application, the claimants have pleaded that the deceased was working with M/s.
Laxmi Borewell, Ambikapur.

The owner however, in the statement though denied that he was regularly employed but however stated that he used to come as and when required and he was paid Rs. 300/- per day as about 10 days he was working with the owner.
The Insurance Company in its written statement had stated that he was the employee of boring machine and not of the insured/offending vehicle and he was traveling as a gratuitous passenger.
In the statement of Birbal Toppo, in cross- examination of the Insurance Company, he has stated that the deceased was working as Helper in the boring machine.

When a specified question was put by the Insurance Company that whether the deceased was working as Khalassy/cleaner in the offending truck, the answer was given by the witness as he was working as cleaner of the Truck ( "og gsYij dk dke djrk Fkk ,slk rks dqN dgrs gSA ")

Though in the cross-examination of the witness Om Prakash Minj The Branch Manager, The Oriental ... vs Birbal Toppo on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153883432/
3 (AW-2), a suggestion was put by the Insurance Company that in the boring machine three labourers were working including the deceased but that Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:25617 is not sufficient enough to suggest that he was not an employee in the boring machine.

entities.text: Om Prakash Minj The Branch Manager, The Oriental ... vs Birbal Toppo
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A person who is employed in the offending vehicle can also come as employee of the boring machine.

Thereafter the learned Tribunal put a question to this witness that whether the deceased was working as a labour in the boring machine truck or as a cleaner, the answer was given that he used to work in both the machine as well as the truck.

The owner himself was examined in paragraph 4 of his affidavit under Order 18 Rule 4 CPC and stated that apart from the driver of the offending vehicle, the deceased as a cleaner and Om Prakash Minj (AW-3) were sitting and in the cross examination in para 9 he has admitted the fact that the deceased was working a cleaner in the offending vehicle.
The Insurance Company has examined witness namely Ankit (NAW-2).
On perusal of the statement, it is not evident from the record that the plea of gratuitous passenger was stated by him in his statement by the learned Tribunal.
He had simply stated that the vehicle was insured and Rs. 150/- was charged as a premium for driver, cleaner.

There is no whisper to the fact that there is a violation of any condition of the policy or the deceased was not the employee in the offending truck as a cleaner or he was travelling as a gratuitous passenger.

13. In view of the above, in the opinion of this Court the appellant/insurance Company could not prove the fact that the deceased was working as an employee of the boring machine rather it appears from the cumulative assessment of the evidence that he was working as a cleaner in the offending vehicle in which the boring machine was also attached.

It is a well settled position of law that once the Insurance Company takes a plea of breach of policy or non- Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:25617 coverage of any person as a gratuitous passenger, by way of cogent and prudent evidence, it is required to discharge its burden.
16. Even from perusal of the statement of NAW-2 Ankit Gupta, nothing is reflected that his defence was proved by the witness.
Even from perusal of the statement of other witnesses, it is established that deceased was working as cleaner in the offending truck.
The case law which has been cited by the learned counsels in any way does not help in any manner or in all distinguishable in the present case.
17. Admittedly, the premium was charged for covering the risk of the deceased and therefore the Insurance Company cannot escape.
So far as the submission made with regard to more number of persons travelling in the offending vehicle is concerned
, from the written statement of the Insurance company, it does not appear that such defence was taken by it rather it has been stated by the witnesses.
Therefore the submission is also liable to be rejected.
18. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the case, the appeal is liable to be and is hereby dismissed.

Sd/-
